models.method_details: OLS cross-sectional regression of the natural log of the absolute performance-adjusted discretionary-current-accrual measure on one fee metric and the listed controls.

dependent_variable.name: ln |PADCA|
dependent_variable.definition: Natural logarithm of the absolute value of Portfolio Performance-Adjusted Discretionary Current Accruals (PADCA). PADCA is DCA minus the median DCA in the same two-digit SIC by prior-year ROA-decile portfolio, with the focal firm excluded; DCA = CA − ECA, and PADCA is deflated by assets.
dependent_variable.formula: ln(|PADCA_i|); PADCA_i = DCA_i − median(DCA_j in same two-digit SIC × prior-year ROA decile portfolio, j ≠ i); DCA = CA − ECA; ECA = αhat_1*(1/Lag1asset) + αhat_2*(ΔRev − ΔAR); CA = (Compustat item 123 + item 125 − item 308) / beginning-of-year total assets. ΔRev and ΔAR are current-minus-prior sales (item 12) and receivables (item 2), each divided by beginning-of-year assets.

scope.quote:
Our first set of tests examine whether FJN’s discretionary accruals results are sensitive
to the measurement of discretionary accruals. Recent research suggests that the discretionary
accrual measure used by FJN systematically rejects the null hypothesis of no-biased financial reporting at much higher-than-stated rates because the measure does not account for
the impact of performance on accruals (Kothari et al. 2002). We calculate two measures of
discretionary current accruals that control for the impact of firm performance in the estimation of discretionary accruals. The first method measures performance-adjusted discretionary current accruals as the difference between a firm’s estimated d

We calculate two measures of
discretionary current accruals that control for the impact of firm performance in the estimation of discretionary accruals. The first method measures performance-adjusted discretionary current accruals as the difference between a firm’s estimated discretionary current
accruals and the median discretionary current accruals from an industry- and performancematched portfolio. The second approach follows Kothari et al. (2002) and includes a control
for firm performance in the regression model used to estimate nondiscretionary current
accruals.

the impact of performance on accruals (Kothari et al. 2002). We calculate two measures of

scope.quote:
Our first set of tests examine whether FJN’s discretionary accruals results are sensitive
to the measurement of discretionary accruals. Recent research suggests that the discretionary
accrual measure used by FJN systematically rejects the null hypothesis of no-biased financial reporting at much higher-than-stated rates because the measure does not account for
the impact of performance on accruals (Kothari et al. 2002). We calculate two measures of
discretionary current accruals that control for the impact of firm performance in the estimation of discretionary accruals. The first method measures performance-adjusted discretionary current accruals as the difference between a firm’s estimated d

We calculate two measures of
discretionary current accruals that control for the impact of firm performance in the estimation of discretionary accruals. The first method measures performance-adjusted discretionary current accruals as the difference between a firm’s estimated discretionary current
accruals and the median discretionary current accruals from an industry- and performancematched portfolio. The second approach follows Kothari et al. (2002) and includes a control
for firm performance in the regression model used to estimate nondiscretionary current
accruals.

Consistent with FJN, we document a positive association between the absolute value
of firms’ discretionary current accruals

scope.quote:

to the measurement of discretionary accruals. Recent research suggests that the discretionary
accrual measure used by FJN systematically rejects the null hypothesis of no-biased financial reporting at much higher-than-stated rates because the measure does not account for
the impact of performance on accruals (Kothari et al. 2002). We calculate two measures of
discretionary current accruals that control for the impact of firm performance in the estimation of discretionary accruals. The first method measures performance-adjusted discretionary current accruals as the difference between a firm’s estimated d

We calculate two measures of

accruals and the median discretionary current accruals from an industry- and performancematched portfolio. The second approach follows Kothari et al. (2002) and includes a control
for firm performance in the regression model used to estimate nondiscretionary current
accruals.

dependent_variable.definition: Natural logarithm of the absolute value of ROA-in-Estimation Discretionary Current Accruals (REDCA). REDCA = CA − ECAPC, where Equation (4) estimates current accruals with lagged ROA and Equation (5) forms expected current accruals; the measure is deflated by assets.
dependent_variable.formula: ln(|REDCA|); REDCA = CA − ECAPC; ECAPC = γhat_1*(1/Lag1asset) + γhat_2*(ΔRev − ΔAR) + γhat_3*Lag1ROA; CA = (Compustat item 123 + item 125 − item 308) / beginning-of-year total assets. ΔRev and ΔAR are current-minus-prior sales (item 12) and receivables (item 2), each divided by beginning-of-year assets; Lag1ROA is prior-year ROA.

evidence.quote:

by including lagged ROA in the accruals regression to control for firm performance. Kothari

and the performance metric. The calculation of REDCA begins by estimating the following

scope.quote:

to the measurement of discretionary accruals. Recent research suggests that the discretionary

the impact of performance on accruals (Kothari et al. 2002). We calculate two measures of

We calculate two measures of

for firm performance in the regression model used to estimate nondiscretionary current

dependent_variable.formula: ln(|REDCA|); REDCA = CA − ECAPC; ECAPC = γhat_1*(1/Lag1asset) + γhat_2*(ΔRev − ΔAR) + γhat_3*Lag1ROA; CA = (Compustat item 123 + item 125 − item 308) / beginning-of-year total assets. scope.quote:
Our first set of tests examine whether FJN’s discretionary accruals results are sensitive
to the measurement of discretionary accruals. Recent research suggests that the discretionary
accrual measure used by FJN systematically rejects the null hypothesis of no-biased financial reporting at much higher-than-stated rates because the measure does not account for
the impact of performance on accruals (Kothari et al. 2002). We calculate two measures of
discretionary current accruals that control for the impact of firm performance in the estimation of discretionary accruals. The first method measures performance-adjusted discretionary current accruals as the difference between a firm’s estimated d

We calculate two measures of
discretionary current accruals that control for the impact of firm performance in the estimation of discretionary accruals. The first method measures performance-adjusted discretionary current accruals as the difference between a firm’s estimated discretionary current
accruals and the median discretionary current accruals from an industry- and performancematched portfolio. The second approach follows Kothari et al. (2002) and includes a control
for firm performance in the regression model used to estimate nondiscretionary current
accruals.

review_notes: Principal question: whether auditor fees are associated with biased financial reporting and thus auditor independence. Retain the full-sample discretionary-accrual models in Table 4 (PADCA and REDCA crossed with four fee metrics) and the full-sample earnings-benchmark models in Tables 7–8 (SURPRISE and INCREASE crossed with the same four fee metrics). The source explicitly identifies discretionary accruals and earnings benchmarks as proxies for biased financial reporting and presents the benchmark models as its second test set (pp. 2–3, 20–21).

Applied the supplied scope clarification before checking prior results: select models that answer the principal question, then include substantive measures supporting that question. PADCA and REDCA construction fits are supporting models; the direct fee-association regressions using them remain baseline models. The PADCA fit also supports the benchmark regressions, where the source adds PADCA as a control.

Table 5 signed-accrual partitions, Table 6 Big 5/non-Big 5 partitions, and the Big 5-only columns of Tables 7–8 are subgroup/follow-up analyses. Table 9 market-reaction models test a separate stock-return response; Table 2 fee-determinant regressions test a different question. These are excluded. The earlier result omitted Tables 7–8; this sweep adds their eight full-sample specifications.

Supplied coordinator-verified transcriptions resolve Equations (2)–(6), including DeltaRev/DeltaAR scaling and lagged ROA timing. The underlying estimators and exact group-specific N for the two accrual-construction fits are not reported, so those fields remain flagged.
